name: Gmail (Google)
summary: You can connect your own Gmail in under an hour, but letting outside users connect means Google verification. If you need to read or modify mail, that also means a paid third-party security assessment (CASA) that repeats every year. Plan for weeks, not days, and pick scopes before you build.

verdict.label: Hard
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: 30–60 minutes (Testing mode, up to 100 test users)
verdict.timeToProduction: Sensitive scopes only: ~1–3 weeks. Restricted scopes (read/modify mail): typically 4–8+ weeks
verdict.approvalWait: Google says sensitive-scope review can take up to 10 days; restricted scopes can take several weeks plus the security assessment. Community reports of 5–8+ week stalls are common.
verdict.handsOnEffort: 1–2 days of prep (policy pages, domain verification, demo video, justifications); more if the assessment finds issues

decideFirst.question: Are all your users inside one Google Workspace organization?
decideFirst.guidance: If yes, set the user type to Internal. Internal apps skip verification, the 100-user cap, and the 7-day token expiry. Most agent products serve outside users, so they need External.

decideFirst.question: Which Gmail scopes do you actually need?
decideFirst.guidance: This one choice sets your timeline. Sending only (gmail.send) is Sensitive: verification with a demo video, no security assessment. Reading, modifying, or drafting mail (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, mail.google.com) is Restricted: verification plus an annual CASA assessment. Labels-only is Non-sensitive.

evidence.note: One widely read third-party article classifies gmail.readonly as Sensitive. Google's own Gmail scopes page lists it as Restricted (read 12 Nov 2026).

decideFirst.question: Do you need your own OAuth app at all?
decideFirst.guidance: If you use a managed-auth platform (e.g. Composio), it may already provide a verified Google app. You still need your own if you want your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes, or your own quota.

phases.name: 1 · Get a working connection (Testing)
phases.goal: Connect your own and your team's accounts

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Use a dedicated project for this integration. The 100-user cap applies per project for its lifetime and cannot be reset.

steps.title: Configure branding and audience (Google Auth Platform)
steps.detail: App name, support email, logo, homepage, privacy policy URL, authorized domains. Choose External and leave it in Testing for now. Add test users (max 100).

steps.title: Declare the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Add only the scopes your code requests. If the scopes requested at runtime differ from the ones declared, users see the unverified-app screen.

steps.title: Create a Web OAuth client and register redirect URIs
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and secret into your secret store. The agent can generate the callback handler and run a test sign-in against localhost.

steps.title: Run an end-to-end test
steps.detail: An agent can write the token exchange and refresh code and test it. Expect the 'Google hasn't verified this app' warning in Testing; that is normal.

phases.name: 2 · Prepare for verification
phases.goal: Have a submission that passes on the first try

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
steps.detail: Use an account that is Owner or Editor on the Cloud project. Every domain on the consent screen must be verified, including redirect URI domains.

evidence.note: Search Console domain verification is on Google's page. The Owner/Editor and redirect-URI details come from a secondary source.

steps.title: Publish homepage and privacy policy on that domain
steps.detail: The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage, linked from the homepage, and disclose how you use Google user data, including the Limited Use disclosure. An agent can draft the Google-specific sections, but have a human or lawyer approve them.

steps.title: Write a justification for each scope
steps.detail: Explain the feature that needs the scope and why a narrower scope will not work. The agent can draft these from your feature list.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the consent screen with your app name, the OAuth client ID in the address bar, and every requested scope in use. The agent can write the shot list; you record it.

steps.title: Publish the app ('In production') and submit in the Verification Center
steps.detail: Track status there. Watch the developer-contact inbox for messages from Trust & Safety, and reply quickly. Every round trip adds days.

steps.title: Google reviews brand + scope use
steps.detail: Brand verification can happen as part of sensitive-scope verification.

steps.title: Restricted scopes only: complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Needed if restricted data is stored on, or passes through, your servers. Google tells you when to start. You hire a Google-approved assessor (fees range from a few hundred to a few thousand USD), fix any findings, and get a Letter of Validation. This repeats every 12 months.

evidence.note: The assessment and its 12-month cadence are on Google's restricted-scope page. The fee range is not; it comes from a different Google page.

requirements.item: Verified domain (Search Console) for homepage, policy and redirect URIs

evidence.note: Google's page says to verify your project's authorized domains. That redirect-URI domains count comes from a secondary source.

requirements.item: Privacy policy on the same domain as the homepage, with the Google user-data / Limited Use disclosure
Third-party CASA security assessment at least every 12 months (Letter of Validation)
requirements.requiredFor: Restricted scopes, if you store or transmit the data on servers

requirements.item: Consistent app name, logo and support email across app, site and submission

scopeTiers.examples: gmail.labels, plus the sign-in scopes openid, email, profile
scopeTiers.consequence: Basic verification at most; no demo video

evidence.note: gmail.labels is listed as Non-sensitive on Google's Gmail scopes page. What review it triggers comes from secondary sources.

scopeTiers.consequence: Verification with justification + demo video. No security assessment.

scopeTiers.examples: mail.google.com, gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, gmail.insert, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing
scopeTiers.consequence: Verification, plus a CASA security assessment at least every 12 months if the data is stored on or passes through your servers

evidence.note: Gmail has no narrow 'only these messages' scope comparable to Drive's drive.file.

blockers.symptom: Tokens stop working exactly 7 days after users connect
blockers.cause: The app is External and still in Testing. Refresh tokens issued in Testing expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Publish to In production (you can do this before verification is done), or use Internal for single-org use.

blockers.cause: In Testing, the user is not on the test-user list
blockers.fix: Add them as a test user (max 100) or publish and verify.

blockers.symptom: Stuck in 'Privacy policy review' for weeks with no email
blockers.cause: This is a common community report. The cause is often unclear.
blockers.fix: Check the developer-contact email and spam folder. Confirm the policy is public with no login, on the verified domain, and includes the Limited Use disclosure. Post on the Google developer forum with your project number.

blockers.cause: Refresh tokens with Gmail scopes are revoked when the user changes their password
blockers.fix: Detect invalid_grant and send the user back through the connect flow.

blockers.cause: The Workspace admin restricts unverified third-party apps or high-risk scopes
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to allowlist your client ID, or finish verification.

nuances.title: The 100-user cap counts for the project's whole lifetime
nuances.detail: Creating a new OAuth client in the same project does not reset it.

nuances.title: Adding a restricted scope later means another review
nuances.detail: Your timeline resets for that scope, and the assessment may need to be expanded.

evidence.note: Not stated in these words on the page we read; inferred from how verification is tied to the scopes you request.

nuances.title: Official timelines and real experience differ
nuances.detail: Google's sensitive-scope page says up to 10 days. Forum threads from 2026 describe 5–8 week stalls. Use 2–4 weeks for planning.

Read in full on 12 Nov 2026: Google's Gmail scopes page. Confirmed the tier of every scope named in this guide: gmail.labels is Non-sensitive, gmail.send is Sensitive, and the eight read/modify/settings scopes are Restricted.

Read in full on 12 Nov 2026: Google's restricted-scope page. Confirmed 'several weeks', CASA as the framework, and an assessment at least every 12 months when restricted data is stored on or sent through your servers.

The first version said restricted scopes always need the assessment. Google's page ties it to storing or transmitting the data on servers, so the guide now states that condition.
Confidence lowered from high to medium: the requirements are confirmed, but real review times are not.
